stcv1g: What FX and CFD trading is
9rjk1a: Foreign exchange, usually shortened to FX or forex, is the buying of one currency with another. Banks, companies, travellers and investors all do it, which makes it one of the busiest markets in the world. Prices move all day on weekdays as supply and demand shift.
r80q4q: Most retail traders do not swap currencies the way a traveller does. They use a broker to open a position that gains or loses value as the exchange rate moves. Very often that position is a CFD.
1vcofhq: A CFD, or contract for difference, is an agreement between you and your broker. You never own the thing you are trading. Instead, the broker pays you the difference if the price moves your way, and you pay the broker the difference if it moves against you.
u5ji9u: CFDs are not limited to currencies. Brokers offer them on stock indices, individual shares, gold, oil and other markets. The same idea applies to all of them: you are exposed to price changes without owning the underlying asset.
gpqket: Buying, or going long, means you gain if the price rises and lose if it falls.
6fiqfb: Selling, or going short, means you gain if the price falls and lose if it rises.
sk2tav: Being able to sell first is one reason CFDs are popular, and also one reason they need care.

13f90s7: CFDs are complex and most retail accounts lose money trading them. This guide explains how they work. It does not suggest that you should trade.

1ldco7c: Currencies are always priced in pairs, because you are measuring one against another. In the pair EUR/USD, the euro is the base currency and the US dollar is the quote currency.
1ttb14z: A price of 1.0850 for EUR/USD means one euro costs 1.0850 US dollars. If the price rises to 1.0900, the euro has strengthened against the dollar. If it falls to 1.0800, the euro has weakened.
h4kdye: Major pairs include the US dollar and another widely traded currency, such as EUR/USD, GBP/USD and USD/JPY.
qkxgji: Minor pairs, sometimes called crosses, leave out the US dollar, such as EUR/GBP or AUD/JPY.
1dvwrww: Exotic pairs combine a major currency with one from a smaller or emerging economy. They often cost more to trade and can move sharply.
16enret: A broker shows two prices for every market. The bid is the price at which you can sell. The ask, sometimes called the offer, is the price at which you can buy. The ask is always a little higher than the bid.
